title: Plan Desk Policy on Open Alignment Work Orders — Alignment Services & Plans Labor and Service Basis
content:
## Policy

A store that performs an alignment on a vehicle holding an Alignment Services & Plans plan posts the work order on the plan with its work-order date, odometer and alignment type, and leaves its service basis open (none) together with a labor charge of 0.00. That work order is the **open work order** of the plan, and the plan desk sets its labor and its service basis.

**Scope.** This policy prices the open work order of a Crestline 1-Year Alignment Plan, Crestline 3-Year Alignment Plan or lifetime plan (Crestline Lifetime Alignment Plan, Crestline Lifetime Alignment Plan Truck & Performance) whose vehicle is in personal use on the visit date. A vehicle in commercial use on the visit date is priced under the commercial-use rule, and a later alignment on a single service is charged under the single-service rule; both are outside this policy.

**Booking the result.** For the open work order of a plan that this policy prices, and only for such a work order, the labor charged is the labor amount this policy prices for the visit, and the work order is booked as `plan_included` when that amount is 0.00 and as `member_early_price` otherwise; a `member_early_price` alignment restarts the interval when the line's member early price counts toward the interval. The purchase-day alignment is `plan_included` with a labor charge of 0.00, and every other alignment that is not priced as an open work order is `plan_included`, with a labor charge of 0.00, when the interval measured from the last interval alignment has been reached (whichever of the month and mile intervals comes first), and is charged the line's member early-alignment price as `member_early_price` before the interval is reached, which restarts the interval when the line's member early price counts toward the interval.

| Labor amount priced for the visit | Service basis booked |
|---|---|
| 0.00 | `plan_included` |
| any amount above 0.00 | `member_early_price` |

## Pricing action: `price_alignment_work_order_228c355b`

**Capability.** Sets the labor of an open alignment work order on a plan: it fills in how the alignment is paid and the labor amount charged for it. On success the work order shows the service basis and labor charge given, which the customer sees on the ticket; its date, odometer, alignment type and parts charge are left as they are.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `price_alignment_work_order_228c355b` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**
- `alignment_plan_id` — reference number of the alignment plan the work order is posted on, taken from the alignment plan lookup (text).
- `alignment_event_id` — reference number of the open alignment work order, an alignment performed entry on the plan whose service basis is none, taken from the plan's alignment activity lookup (text).
- `service_basis` — how the alignment is paid; accepted values: `plan_included` (no labor is charged because the alignment is included in the plan) and `member_early_price` (labor is charged for this alignment). The values `none` and `guarantee_readjustment` are not accepted here.
- `charge_amount` — labor charged for the alignment, in USD, a non-negative amount with 2 decimal places; the tool rounds to the nearest cent when more digits are given; 0.00 when nothing is charged.

**Return.** A text rendering of a dictionary with `alignment_plan_id`, `alignment_event_id`, `service_basis` (the basis now booked), `charge_amount` (the labor now booked, USD with 2 decimal places) and `status` with the text `priced`, confirming the work order now carries its labor. A `service_basis` outside the accepted values returns a text starting with "Error:" and changes nothing.

*Illustration (hypothetical references):* a call for plan AP-1 and work order WO-7 with `service_basis` `member_early_price` and `charge_amount` 12.346 books 12.35 and returns status `priced`.
